title: Theme
summary: A work's abstract meaning, carried by the concretes the artist chose.

lessons.title: What a theme is
lessons.objective: Name a theme as the work's abstract meaning, and reject substitutes that are not a meaning at all.

exercises.prompt: What is a theme?

choices.text: The work's abstract meaning
The list of events in order
How skilled the artist is
What the work sold for

feedback.note: A theme is the work's abstract meaning, not a record of events, a rating of skill, or a market fact.

exercises.prompt: Match each phrase to what it names in a work.

pairs.left: Theme
Concretes
Carrier

feedback.note: The theme is the meaning. The concretes are what the artist put in. They are what carry the meaning.

exercises.prompt: Complete the name of a theme.

feedback.note: Abstract means the meaning is a general idea, not one isolated fact sitting beside the work.

exercises.prompt: Build the unit's claim in order.

feedback.note: Keep both parts: the theme is abstract meaning, and that meaning is carried by the concretes.

exercises.prompt: Which of these could be a theme?

choices.text: A person can remake a life by choice
The story has three named people
The book is two hundred pages
The cover is blue

feedback.note: A theme is a meaning you can state in general terms. A head count, a length, or a color is not a meaning.

exercises.prompt: Match each candidate to theme or not a theme.

pairs.left: Justice can fail when people look away
Chapter four is the longest
The painting uses oil

feedback.note: Only the first item states an abstract meaning. Length and medium are facts about the object, not its theme.

exercises.prompt: Fill the two words that name what a theme is.

feedback.note: Those two words are the core. Everything else in the unit says how that meaning gets into the work.

exercises.prompt: A theme belongs to which of these?

choices.text: The work, as its abstract meaning
Only the loudest fan's mood
The shelf the book sits on
The price of a ticket

feedback.note: The theme is the work's meaning. A viewer's mood or a price tag is not a substitute for it.

lessons.title: Not a plot summary
lessons.objective: Tell a theme apart from a retelling of the events, characters, or surface details.

exercises.prompt: A plot summary mainly reports what?

choices.text: What happens, in the concretes
The abstract meaning those events carry
Which esthetic school the artist joined
Whether you agree with the artist

feedback.note: A summary stays with the events. A theme states the abstract meaning those events are there to carry.

exercises.prompt: Match each sentence to plot or theme.

pairs.left: She leaves the town after the trial
Integrity can cost a place in the group
He finds the letter in the desk

feedback.note: Leaving, a trial, and a letter are concretes. Integrity and its cost are the kind of meaning a theme states.

exercises.prompt: Complete the contrast.

parts.text: A plot recounts events. A theme states

feedback.note: Do not stop at what happened. Ask what abstract meaning those happenings carry.

exercises.prompt: Order the contrast.

feedback.note: Plot answers what happens. Theme answers what that sequence means in abstract terms.

exercises.prompt: Someone says the theme is that the hero crosses a river. What went wrong?

choices.text: That names an event, not an abstract meaning
Nothing. An event is already a theme
The sentence is too short to be a plot
A theme must include the hero's name

feedback.note: Crossing a river is a concrete event. The theme would be the abstract meaning that crossing is used to carry.

exercises.prompt: Match the question to the answer it seeks.

pairs.left: What happens?
What does it mean?
Who is on stage?

feedback.note: Who appears and what they do are concretes. The theme is the meaning those choices carry.

exercises.prompt: Two works share the same chase scene. Must they share a theme?

choices.text: No. The same kind of event can carry different meanings
Yes. Matching events fix the theme
Only if both works are short
No event can carry any meaning

feedback.note: A chase is a concrete. What it means depends on the meaning the whole choice of concretes carries.

exercises.prompt: Finish the warning.

parts.text: Retelling the events is not yet stating the

feedback.note: A retelling stays at the concretes. The theme is the abstract meaning those concretes carry.

exercises.prompt: Which line is closer to a theme than to a plot note?

choices.text: Courage is acting when the outcome is not guaranteed
She opens the door at midnight
It rains in chapter two
He wears a gray hat

feedback.note: The first line states an abstract meaning. The others report details a plot summary might include.

lessons.title: The concretes chosen
lessons.objective: Identify the concretes as the particulars the artist chose, which are what carry the theme.

exercises.prompt: In this unit, what carries the theme?

choices.text: The concretes the artist chose
A preface written by someone else
A review printed later
The shipping crate

feedback.note: The theme is carried by the concretes the artist chose, not by packaging or by a later comment.

exercises.prompt: Match each concrete to the art it could belong to.

pairs.left: A named action in a story
A figure placed in a painting
A musical phrase set against silence

feedback.note: Concretes differ by art. In each case they are the particulars the artist chose to carry the meaning.

exercises.prompt: Complete the carrier.

parts.text: The theme is carried by the

feedback.note: Chosen concretes are the carrier. Outside talk about the work is not a substitute carrier.

exercises.prompt: Build the relation.

feedback.note: Choice of concretes and the meaning they carry belong together. The theme is not parked outside the work.

exercises.prompt: Why say the artist chose the concretes?

choices.text: The particulars in the work are there by the artist's selection
Every fact in the world is automatically in the work
Concretes appear with no one deciding
The audience inserts the concretes later

feedback.note: A work does not contain everything. The concretes that carry the theme are the ones the artist chose.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to inside the work or outside it.

pairs.left: The action the story shows
A friend's summary at dinner
The image the painting presents

feedback.note: Only what the artist put into the work is a concrete that can carry its theme. Talk about the work is not the work.

exercises.prompt: An artist drops a scene that pointed another way. What changed?

choices.text: The set of concretes that carry the meaning
Nothing, because theme ignores concretes
The legal status of the audience
The calendar year of the reader's birth

feedback.note: Leaving a scene out changes which concretes are there to carry the theme. The carrier is the set the artist kept.

exercises.prompt: Fill both blanks.

feedback.note: Meaning is the theme. Concretes are the carrier. Both words are required.

exercises.prompt: Which list is a list of concretes rather than a theme?

choices.text: A bridge, a storm, and a refusal to turn back
Resolve holds when conditions turn against you
Both lines are themes
Neither line has anything to do with a work

feedback.note: Bridge, storm, and refusal are particulars. The sentence about resolve is the kind of abstract meaning they might carry.

lessons.title: Carried, not pasted on
lessons.objective: Hold that the theme is carried by the concretes, not supplied by a slogan attached beside them.

exercises.prompt: A poster beside a painting says what the painting means, but the image shows none of it. Where is the theme of the painting?

choices.text: Only in what the image's concretes actually carry
In the poster, which replaces the image
The poster becomes part of the painting automatically
Paintings cannot have a theme

feedback.note: A slogan next to the work is not the carrier. The theme has to be carried by the concretes the artist chose.

exercises.prompt: Match each case to carried or merely pasted.

pairs.left: The actions show the meaning the author names
A last sentence announces a meaning the story never shows
A caption states a moral the picture does not present

feedback.note: Carried means the concretes present the meaning. Pasted means the meaning is only announced from outside those concretes.

exercises.prompt: Complete the standard.

feedback.note: Carried is the verb in this unit. A meaning that the concretes do not carry is not the work's theme.

exercises.prompt: Order the check.

feedback.note: Start from the chosen concretes. The theme is the abstract meaning they carry, not a line attached later.

exercises.prompt: The artist can state the theme in an essay. Does that statement replace the work?

choices.text: No. In the work, the concretes still have to carry it
Yes. An essay is the theme of every work by that artist
Only if the essay is shorter than the work
No artist may say what a work means

feedback.note: An outside statement can name a meaning. Inside the work, that meaning still has to be carried by the concretes.

exercises.prompt: A story's events all show betrayal, and the last line says the theme is loyalty. Which meaning did the concretes carry?

choices.text: Betrayal, the meaning the events present
Loyalty, because the last line says so
Both equally, with no role for the events
Neither, because stories have no theme

feedback.note: When the announcement and the concretes conflict, the theme of the work is the meaning the concretes carry.

exercises.prompt: Match the mistake to what it confuses.

pairs.left: Treating a plot note as the theme
Treating a slogan as the theme
Treating a review as the theme
pairs.right: Outside talk instead of the work

feedback.note: The theme is abstract meaning, and it is carried by the work's own concretes. Events, slogans, and reviews each miss one of those.

exercises.prompt: Finish the contrast.

parts.text: A pasted slogan is not a substitute for meaning

feedback.note: Pasting a moral beside the work does not make that moral the theme. The concretes have to carry it.

lessons.title: One claim
lessons.objective: Apply the full claim: a theme is the work's abstract meaning, and that meaning is carried by the concretes the artist chose.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence states this unit's full claim?

choices.text: A theme is the work's abstract meaning, carried by the concretes the artist chose
A theme is whatever a reviewer feels that day
A theme is the order of chapters
A theme is a sense of life, and nothing further

feedback.note: Keep both halves. Abstract meaning names the theme. The chosen concretes are what carry it.

exercises.prompt: Match each half of the claim to its job.

pairs.left: Abstract meaning
Chosen concretes
A slogan beside the work

feedback.note: The two halves answer different questions: what the meaning is, and what in the work carries it.

exercises.prompt: Assemble the full claim.

feedback.note: Drop the distractors. The claim is meaning plus the concretes that carry it, not a review and not the plot.

exercises.prompt: Complete both halves.

parts.text: , carried by the concretes the artist

feedback.note: Meaning names the theme. Chose names the artist's selection of the concretes that carry it.

exercises.prompt: A reader reports only the events and never the meaning. What is missing?

choices.text: The theme, the abstract meaning those events carry
The events, which were never mentioned
The sale price
The name of an esthetic school

feedback.note: Events are the concretes. Without the abstract meaning they carry, the theme has not been stated.

exercises.prompt: A reader states a grand meaning and never looks at what the artist put in the work. What is missing?

choices.text: The concretes that would have to carry that meaning
Nothing, because a meaning needs no carrier
The typeface of the title
The city where the reader lives

feedback.note: An abstract meaning becomes the work's theme only as what the chosen concretes carry.

exercises.prompt: Match the reader's move to the verdict.

pairs.left: States a meaning the concretes carry
Stops at a list of events
pairs.right: Has the plot, not the theme

pairs.left: Quotes a slogan the work does not present
pairs.right: Has a paste-on, not the theme

feedback.note: Only the first move keeps abstract meaning and the chosen concretes together.

exercises.prompt: One last completion.

parts.text: The theme is not the plot and not a slogan. It is

feedback.note: That is the whole unit: abstract meaning, carried by the concretes the artist chose.

exercises.prompt: Two readers name the same abstract meaning. One can point to the concretes that carry it. The other cannot. Who has shown the theme of this work?

choices.text: The reader who ties the meaning to the chosen concretes
The reader who only announces the meaning
Neither, because a theme cannot be shown
Both equally, because concretes do not matter

feedback.note: Showing the theme means showing the abstract meaning as what these concretes carry, not merely saying a general idea.

exercises.prompt: Put the check in the order this unit uses.

tokens.text: Point to the concretes that carry it

feedback.note: First the meaning, then the concretes that carry it. A poster or a refusal to look at the work does not complete the claim.
